sections.approach: Our programme takes a balanced, educationally justified approach to AI.

sectionBasis.approach: The programme team has considered how Generative AI is affecting the discipline and the professional practice that graduates will enter. Generative AI is reshaping analyst and consultancy roles: routine reporting, documentation and first-draft code are increasingly automated, while employers expect graduates to specify, evaluate and govern AI-enabled systems. The programme has adopted a selectively AI-integrated approach. AI is integrated where it mirrors professional analyst practice and restricted where foundational knowledge or client communication must be demonstrated independently.

statement.agreedSnapshot:
Our Approach to AI
Our programme takes a balanced, educationally justified approach to AI.

Graduate Capabilities
Capabilities that graduates must be able to demonstrate independently of AI include foundational disciplinary knowledge, critical thinking, professional judgement and interpersonal communication. Capabilities that graduates should develop for using AI effectively, critically and responsibly include selecting appropriate AI tools, evaluating AI-generated outputs, responsible and ethical AI use, integrating AI into disciplinary workflows and documenting or communicating AI use. Add an explicit programme outcome on responsible AI-enabled practice.

Curriculum and Assessment
The programme’s AI capability progression map (I introduced, P practised, E extended, D demonstrated) records: AI literacy and responsible use: Stage 1 (I, P); Critical evaluation of AI outputs: Stage 2 (I), Stage 3 (E); Discipline-specific AI application: Stage 3 (I, P), Stage 4 (E, D); Human judgement and oversight: Stage 3 (I), Stage 4 (D); Effective human–AI collaboration: Stage 2 (I, P). [Some progression entries were carried over from an earlier review and have not yet been confirmed] [How does the programme provide appropriate assurance of student learning?] Module reviews describe AI-restricted assessment in BIS101 (end-of-semester examination), AI-limited or bounded assessment in BIS101 (business report) and AI-integrated assessment in BIS301 (client project with presentation).

Responsible AI
Graduates are expected to develop capabilities in evaluating AI-generated outputs, responsible and ethical AI use and documenting or communicating AI use. AI literacy and responsible use, critical evaluation of AI outputs and human judgement and oversight are developed across the stages of the programme, as shown in the progression map.

Review and Development
Strengths identified in the review include: Stage 3 and 4 project work already integrates AI with strong assurance through client contact and defence. The programme team’s priorities for development are: (1) review AI guidance for stage 2 group projects. The programme team will review this statement by 1 October 2027.
